To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the histidyl-t RNA synthetase gene was cloned from S. equisimilis and expressed in E. coli as a fusion protein.
we have overexpressed and purified the histidyl-t-RNA synthetase from S. equisimilis and that the enzyme is a dodecamer.
the fusion HisRS is a dimeric enzyme that is active and has an apparent MW of approximately 108,000 Da.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of histidyl-tRNAsynthetase from the gram-positive bacterium S. equisimilis, which is the first report of the expression of this enzyme from a gram-positive organism.
the expression, purification, and initial characterization of the S. equisimilis HisRS.
the overproduction of a histidyl-t RNA synthetase from S. equisimilis in E. coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fusion protein is a dimer with two identical subunits of M(r) approximately 53,700 Da.
the fusion HisRS is composed of two identical sub-units, each with an additional 15 amino acids, which have been added at the amino terminus.
the native HisRS of S. equisimilis is a dimer with a MW of 94,000.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to produce a functional HisRS from S. equisimilis in a high yield.
a high level expression system has been established for this enzyme, and a fusion protein has been obtained which has the same enzymatic and binding properties as the native enzyme.
we have cloned the hisS gene from S. equisimilis, expressed it at a high level in E. coli, and purified the fusion protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have successfully expressed and purified the S. equisimilis HisRS in a heterologous expression system.
the fusion protein is functional and can be purified to homogeneity by a combination of two chromatographic steps.
the S. equisimilis HisRS can be expressed in E. coli at a high level.
